news_summary: A football team demonstrated remarkable resilience and determination by rebuilding and moving forward after the tragic loss of 19 players in a plane crash.

articles.title: How a football team rebuilt after 19 players died in plane crash
articles.summary: How a Brazilian football team rose again after a plane crash that killed most of their players and staff on the way to what should have been the biggest match of their lives.
articles.content:
Seven thousand kilometres away in the small southern Brazilian city of Chapeco, Tozzo watched the scale of the disaster unfold on TV screens at the stadium in the middle of the night.

"At five o'clock in the morning, the players' wives began to arrive. It was despair. People threw themselves on the ground and cried," says Tozzo, a local entrepreneur who was the club's vice-president at the time and had joined the club in 2009 when they were not even playing in Brazil's national football pyramid.

Two days earlier, Tozzo had suffered misgivings about the trip that were so strong that he had changed his mind about travelling to Medellin.

"It was a thing from God. It was not for me to go. I called [financial director] Decio, who organised all our trips, and I told him that I would not go," he says.

"He went crazy with me. 'Why? You agreed to go, now you do not want to go? You have to go.'

"My sister was next to me, saying, 'You need to go to this match, you worked so hard to get to this moment.' But in my head I said, 'No Ivan, I will not go', and I stayed at home."

After the crash, he had another strong feeling about his path.

"I think I had a mission here on Earth to continue Chapecoense after the accident," Tozzo says. "I was the only one of the directors left alive so I took over as [interim] president."

A sleepless week followed in which Tozzo arranged flights to Colombia for doctors, relatives and pastors to identify and recover the remains and be with the survivors.

A memorial service was organised and, in pouring rain, the coffins were brought into Chape's stadium, Arena Conda.

During the service came the news that Atletico Nacional had asked for the Copa Sudamericana trophy and winners' prize money to be awarded to Chapecoense.

Then came the question of the future.

Tozzo was determined Chapecoense would compete again, but none of the surviving players were in any shape to play and they only had two other squad members – who did not travel to Medellin because of injury – and a handful in the academy.

They called on Rui Costa, who had been sacked by Gremio as football director six months earlier and accepted the same role with Chapecoense, and appointed Vagner Mancini as coach.

In a matter of weeks, 22 new players were signed, most of them on loan.

Tozzo's message rang clear in the ears of the new players.

"Our fans were very sad, Chapecoense was very sad, and playing again with joy was not easy," he says.

"We explained very well the responsibility they would have."

It was time to return to the pitch.

articles.personality_title: How a Brazilian football team rebuilt after a tragic plane crash
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In 2016, a plane carrying the Brazilian football team Chapecoense crashed on the way to an important match in Colombia. The crash killed 19 players and staff members, leaving the club devastated.

**What happened** – The club’s vice-president, Ivan Tozzo, did not travel on the plane because he had a strong feeling not to go. After the crash, he became interim president and led the team’s recovery. With only a few players left, they hired a new coach and signed 22 new players quickly to rebuild the team.

**Impact** – The team’s return to playing showed great strength and hope. It was important because the club not only faced a huge loss but also had to rebuild their future from almost nothing. The support from other clubs and the community helped Chapecoense continue its journey.

**What’s next step** – Chapecoense will keep playing in Brazil’s football leagues, honoring those lost by showing commitment and teamwork. The club’s leaders and new players are focused on moving forward while remembering the past.

**One-sentence takeaway** – After losing most of their team in a plane crash, Chapecoense rebuilt quickly with new players and leaders to keep their football dream alive.
articles.personality_title_fr: Comment une équipe brésilienne de football s’est reconstruite après un tragique crash d’avion
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – En 2016, un avion transportant l’équipe brésilienne de football Chapecoense s’est écrasé en route vers un match important en Colombie. Le crash a tué 19 joueurs et membres du personnel, laissant le club dévasté.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Le vice-président du club, Ivan Tozzo, n’a pas pris l’avion car il avait un fort pressentiment. Après le crash, il est devenu président par intérim et a dirigé la reconstruction de l’équipe. Avec seulement quelques joueurs restants, ils ont engagé un nouvel entraîneur et signé rapidement 22 nouveaux joueurs.

**Impact** – Le retour de l’équipe sur le terrain a montré une grande force et de l’espoir. C’était important car le club a dû reconstruire son avenir presque à partir de rien. Le soutien d’autres clubs et de la communauté a aidé Chapecoense à continuer son chemin.

**Prochaine étape** – Chapecoense continuera à jouer dans les championnats brésiliens, honorant ceux qui sont partis en montrant engagement et esprit d’équipe. Les dirigeants et les nouveaux joueurs se concentrent sur l’avenir tout en se souvenant du passé.

**Une phrase clé** – Après avoir perdu la plupart de son équipe dans un crash d’avion, Chapecoense s’est rapidement reconstruite avec de nouveaux joueurs et dirigeants pour garder leur rêve de football vivant.
articles.personality_title_es: Cómo un equipo brasileño de fútbol se reconstruyó tras un trágico accidente aéreo
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En 2016, un avión que llevaba al equipo brasileño de fútbol Chapecoense se estrelló camino a un partido importante en Colombia. El accidente mató a 19 jugadores y miembros del personal, dejando al club devastado.

**Qué pasó** – El vicepresidente del club, Ivan Tozzo, no viajó porque tuvo un fuerte presentimiento. Tras el accidente, se convirtió en presidente interino y lideró la reconstrucción del equipo. Con pocos jugadores restantes, contrataron un nuevo entrenador y ficharon rápidamente a 22 jugadores nuevos.

**Impacto** – El regreso del equipo al campo mostró mucha fuerza y esperanza. Fue importante porque el club tuvo que reconstruir su futuro casi desde cero. El apoyo de otros clubes y la comunidad ayudó a Chapecoense a seguir adelante.

**Próximo paso** – Chapecoense seguirá jugando en las ligas brasileñas, honrando a los que se fueron con compromiso y trabajo en equipo. Los líderes y nuevos jugadores están enfocados en avanzar mientras recuerdan el pasado.

**Una frase clave** – Tras perder a la mayoría de su equipo en un accidente aéreo, Chapecoense se reconstruyó rápidamente con nuevos jugadores y líderes para mantener vivo su sueño futbolístico.
